abort_authority.directive_summary: Hiring is a FULL SaaS PRODUCT (Greenhouse/Ashby-class) at microservices/hiring/. TA Recruiter + Hiring Manager are ROLES INSIDE that B2B product. A separate sibling microservices/job-search-consumer/ µservice exists on the consumer side (LinkedIn job-seeker side), strictly separated from work-context identity per ADR-0135 Connect-unbundle precedent.

verification.note: Agent verified hiring-experience scope in template-grokking phase only; no writes to disk before abort signal received.

b2b_product_microservice.parity_target_class: ATS + sourcing + scheduling + assessment + offer + onboarding-handoff

consumer_side_microservice.separation_basis: ADR-0135 Connect-unbundle precedent (b2b posture vs b2c posture strict split; identity-context segregation)
consumer_side_microservice.primary_user: job-seeker (consumer identity, NOT work-context tenant member)
consumer_side_microservice.parity_target_class: LinkedIn Jobs / Indeed / Glassdoor / ZipRecruiter (seeker-side surface)
explicit_separation_rules: Consumer identity in job-search-consumer never resolves to tenant-member identity in hiring/
Cross-product application bridge flows ONLY through canonical workflow + ontology adapters (per [[workflow-objectgraph-adapter-layer]])
Consumer's job-application event reaches the B2B hiring µservice via an explicit `application-submitted` capability, never via shared DB

correct_target_architecture.strict_separation_rationale: Conforms to feedback_bominal_inheritance_precedence + feedback_flat_product_catalog + feedback_workflow_objectgraph_adapter_layer. Work-context (B2B tenant) and consumer-context (B2C job seeker) are distinct identity domains; merging them duplicates Workday Recruiting's clunky 'one identity for everyone' anti-pattern.

ta_recruiter_pain_points_today: 5 SaaS tools per req (ATS + sourcing + scheduling + assessment + offer letter)
Interview kit drafted by random Notion doc
Calibration done in 3-hour meeting because there's no peer-benchmark data
Onboarding handoff is 'Slack the HR person with new hire info'
hiring_manager_pain_points_today: Req opening requires chasing finance + CFO approvals manually
Candidate review UX is paginated tables across multiple tabs
Debrief turns into a popularity contest because no rubric is shared
Offer approval bottlenecks at CEO because no budget integration

surfaces_to_carry_forward.spec: workflow-driven approval (manager -> finance -> CFO -> CEO) with budget integration; auto-post to LinkedIn / Indeed / etc.; requires shared workflow µservice
candidates by stage, by source, conversion rates per recruiter, time-to-fill; per-tenant filtering; PRD perf bar p99 <= 300 ms
Boolean search + profile enrichment + smart match against JD + competency model; bias-audit + explainability per NYC LL 144 from day 1
from JD + competency model, AI drafts interview questions + rubric per round (technical, behavioral, leadership); rubric-versioned; calibration-bound
peer benchmarks, comp band, equity refresh, total package; comp data isolated per tenant; never shared cross-tenant
from approved package, auto-generates with e-signature workflow; templated per-region per-pack
triggers employee-manager-experience µservice onboarding workflow; zero manual data copy; idempotent handoff event
adapter to Checkr / GoodHire / SterlingCheck; vendor-replaceable Phase-2; consent flow + adverse-action workflow

frameworks: NYC Local Law 144 (AI hiring bias audits)
EU AI Act Annex III §4 (employment AI is HIGH-RISK)
non_negotiable_controls: NYC LL 144: annual independent bias audit + public-results posting + candidate notice
EU AI Act Annex III §4: human oversight + transparency + accuracy + record-keeping + post-market monitoring
EEO-1 / OFCCP: protected-class data segregated; analyzed in aggregate only
ADA: accessible candidate-facing surfaces; reasonable accommodation workflow
Ban-the-box: per-state conditional-offer workflow; criminal-history disclosure gated

anti_patterns_to_refuse: Don't be Greenhouse + great ATS but isolated from rest of HRIS
Don't be Workday Recruiting + clunky UI + slow
Don't ship AI sourcing without bias audit + explainability per NYC LL 144
